paragraphs.text: Searchable project conversation excerpts for DSH
# dsh-recall
DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 plugin. Node >=24; developed and tested locally with Node 26 / TypeScript 5.9.3. Rele
ase CI is configured for Node 24; that CI run is separate from local verification.
## Install from a GitHub Release
After a release is published, install its built archive into your DSH profile:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The release URL is the expected v0.1.0 asset location, not a claim that it has already been publishe
d. Use the archive and SHA256SUMS attached to the same GitHub Release. The package includes a DSH bu
ndle patch and built JavaScript; no Pi dependency is needed. Restart DSH after installation. Substit
ute your existing profile for `headless` if needed.
## Configuration
The default bundle config is `{}`: each tool uses the invoking agent's working directory. A host cal
l without an agent requires an explicit `root`. To pin a host-local workspace, add an override in yo
ur profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The root must already exist. It is interpreted on the DSH host, using Node filesystem APIs. A remote
DSH world or sandbox does not redirect these operations: only enable this plugin for a host-local p
roject. This is not a remote-world adapter or a security sandbox.
## Tools and examples
- `recall_save({role:"user",text:"We chose SQLite for the local cache",sessionId:"optional-source-id
"})` saves only the explicitly provided excerpt. The source ID defaults to the current agent ID, or
`manual` for a host call. Exact duplicate role/text/session combinations return the existing record.
- `recall_search({query:"sqlite cache",limit:10})` performs literal case-insensitive AND matching o
n saved text, newest first. Omit the query to list saved excerpts. Results include `id`, `revision`,

`role`, `text`, `sessionId` and `savedAt`.
- `recall_delete({id:"<result id>",expectedRevision:"<re
sult revision>"})` removes one saved excerpt only when its revision matches. An unknown ID or stale
revision fails explicitly.
Ask DSH: “Explicitly save this decision in recall: we chose SQLite for the local cache.” Later: “Sea
rch recall for sqlite cache.” Excerpts are untrusted quoted conversation data, not instructions. No
session log is automatically searched, copied or summarized. Caller-supplied role/session attributio
n is not independently authenticated.
## Storage and limits
The store lives in `<workspace>/.dsh-recall/records.json`. The directory is created with mode 0700 a
nd replacement files with mode 0600 (subject to filesystem/platform behavior). This is plaintext, no
t encryption: save only material appropriate to keep in this project, exclude `.dsh-recall/` from ve
rsion control, and do not save secrets. This plugin intentionally does not edit your .gitignore.
At most 200 records / 4 MiB total, 50,000 UTF-8 bytes per excerpt, 200 characters per session ID, 50
0 per search query, and a search limit of 1–50. Traversal, symlink storage paths and nonregular file
s are rejected. Malformed stores fail closed; they are never silently reset. Search does not create
storage. Records survive DSH/plugin restarts and are shared across agents using the same local root.
Writers acquire `.dsh-recall/write.lock` exclusively. Concurrent writers fail with “store busy” and
can retry; accepted writes use a fsynced temporary file and atomic rename so readers see a complete
old or new store. Temporary files and locks are removed on normal success/failure. A process crash c
an leave a lock/temp file: stop all writers, inspect/recover the store, then manually remove the sta
le lock/temp. There is no automatic stale-lock stealing or crash-time directory fsync guarantee. Can
cellation is checked before commit and work is drained on dispose; a rename already committed is not
rolled back by a later cancellation.
No Pi picker/menu, global Pi store migration, Markdown notes/templates, automatic session capture, D
SH session-search replacement or automatic prompt injection is provided.
## Filesystem boundary and verification
Path checks reject ordinary symlink redirection; regular-file opens use no-follow flags and inode ch
ecks, bounded reads and cancellation. These checks are not a sandbox against a malicious process con
currently replacing ancestor directories; use a trusted local workspace. Linux/macOS-style filesyste
m semantics are the intended target; Windows behavior has not been verified.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The suite uses real Cordis, DSH ToolRuntime, agent-loop and an offline scripted model; it verifies a
ctual model tool dispatch and results in the following model request, plus limits, revision/path che
cks, cancellation and unregistration. It requires no live model credentials. `check` includes TypeSc
ript checks for source/tests, behavior tests and a build. See UPSTREAM.md for pinned source and migr
ation differences and NOTICE for upstream MIT attribution.
